SingleCellExposomeExperiment: Container for single-cell exposome data

Source: R/AllClasses.R, R/methods.R
SingleCellExposomeExperiment-class.Rd

Extends SingleCellExperiment with sample-level environmental exposure measurements. This enables cell-type-specific exposome-wide association studies (sc-ExWAS).

Usage

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExposomeExperiment,ANY,ANY,ANY'
x[i, j, ..., drop = TRUE]

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExposomeExperiment'
cbind(..., deparse.level = 1)

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExposomeExperiment'
rbind(..., deparse.level = 1)

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExposomeExperiment,DataFrame'
colData(x, ...) <- value

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExposomeExperiment,NULL'
colData(x, ...) <- value

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExposomeExperiment,list'
dimnames(x) <- value

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExposomeExperiment,NULL'
dimnames(x) <- value

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExposomeExperiment'
show(object)

Arguments

x

A SingleCellExposomeExperiment.

i

Row (gene) subscript.

j

Column (cell) subscript.

...

Additional arguments.

drop

Logical. Ignored (kept for S4 compatibility).

deparse.level

Ignored.

value

The replacement colData or dimnames.

object

A SingleCellExposomeExperiment.

Value

The subsetting method returns a valid SingleCellExposomeExperiment. When cells are subset, its exposureData is restricted to the donors that keep at least one cell; feature subsetting leaves the donor-level slots unchanged. cbind combines objects with the same exposure variables, exposure metadata and sample column; donors present in more than one object must have identical exposure values. Every argument to cbind or rbind must be a SingleCellExposomeExperiment: when a plain SingleCellExperiment comes first, R dispatches to the SingleCellExperiment method, which returns a SingleCellExperiment without the exposure data (with only a warning about ambiguous dispatch), so convert such objects with build_scee first. rbind combines objects with the same cells and different features; they must have the same sample column and exposureInfo, and the same exposure values for each donor. The replacement methods return the modified object. The show method is called for its display side effect and returns NULL invisibly.

Details

The donor of each cell is read from one column of colData, whose name is stored in the object (see sampleColumn). The cell-to-donor mapping is not stored a second time, so renaming cells, combining objects and editing colData cannot leave two copies out of step. The object is valid when every donor in that column has exactly one row in exposureData and every row of exposureData belongs to at least one cell.

Replacing colData, or a column of it with $<- or [[<-, checks validity again, so an edit that removes the donor column or introduces a donor without exposure data is an error; so does replacing the cell names with colnames<-. To change donor identifiers, edit exposureData and colData together and rebuild the object with build_scee.

Slots

exposureData

Numeric matrix. Rows = samples (donors), columns = exposure variables.

exposureInfo

DataFrame. Metadata for each exposure (family, unit, LOD).

sampleColumn

Character scalar. Name of the colData column holding each cell's sample (donor) identifier.

Data hierarchy


Donor (n=50-1000)
  |-- Exposures (PM2.5, Pb, BPA, ...)   <- sample level
  +-- Cells x Genes matrix
      |-- T cells (1000 cells)
      |-- NK cells (500 cells)            <- cell level
      +-- Monocytes (800 cells)

References

van der Wijst MGP et al. (2020). The single-cell eQTLGen consortium. eLife 9:e52155. doi:10.7554/eLife.52155
